html_source:
In brief

Simon Dedalus asks Miss Douce if she has "Enjoyed her holidays," adding that he hopes that "she had nice weather in Rostrevor." This seaside village in County Down, Ulster, is not far from "the Mourne mountains," which Simon says he has "often wanted to see."

At more length

Rostrevor (current population 2,800) sits near the head of Carlingford Lough, a long arm of the Irish Sea. A southfacing beach, sandy in places, offers good swimming and sunbathing in fine weather. Miss Douce has been favored with good weather, "Lying out on the strand all day." East and northeast of he village there is also spectacular mountain scenery. The high, bare granite peaks of the Mourne range—Ireland's most famous—lie just beyond the lush Rostrevor Forest.

John Hunt 2025
